shared_elements: low-relief carving on weathered pale stone
horizontal bands/registers of repeated small motifs
monolithic block set outdoors in an excavated/ground context
justification: The clearest correspondence is the use of stacked horizontal registers of repeated, roughly rectangular carved units running the width of the stone, which dominate the upper part of A and effectively all of B. Beyond that they diverge sharply: A is a tall upright slab with crisp, legible figural relief (quadrupeds, birds, human-like figures, discs) below its bands, while B is a low, broad, heavily eroded block whose motifs are shallow, uniform and non-figural as visible, giving a completely different overall impression.
